# Open items, 2026-09-03

This file collects three lists into one: the decisions that are not confirmed (UNSURE), the detours that cost time (PAPERCUTS), and the last open review item.
Each item is written so that you can read it without the old context.
Comment on an item to confirm, reject, or change it.

## Part 1. Decisions that wait for a verdict

Each item says what the code does now, what the other option was, and why we chose.

### Comments and anchors

- A comment on a body line is stored by line number and by the text of that line.
  When the text moves to a different line, the comment follows it.
  When the text is gone, the comment stays on the old line number, and the screen gives no hint.
  The moved position is not written back to the json.
  Other option: a "drifted" flag and a dimmed gutter glyph.
  Why: nobody hit this yet, and a reload must not change the store.
- A comment on a heading line is stored by the heading path, not by line number.
  Body lines are not tied to their heading.
  Other option: tie each body line to its heading plus an offset.
- Comments live in one json per document under the data directory (`$MDTATION_HOME`, `$XDG_DATA_HOME/mdtation`, or `~/.mdtation`), named by the absolute path.
  An append-only events log lives next to it.
  Other option: sqlite, or a sidecar file next to the markdown.
  Why: zero dependencies, one file to inspect, no hidden folder next to every markdown file.
- Archive is a per-comment timestamp in the same json.
  Marks (checkpoints for `--since last`) live in the same json too.
  Other option: derive "archived" from the last mark.
  Why: `archive <id>` and the retention sweep need a fact per comment.
- Comments archived before the timestamp existed count from their creation date.
  There is no migration code.
- The default retention for archived comments is 30 days.
  The sweep runs only when the TUI starts, not on `list`.
  Other option: never delete, or 7 days.
- A comment from the TUI has no author name.
  The CLI uses `$USER` for the human and `$MDTATION_AUTHOR` for the agent.
  Other option: a name setting in the settings file.
  Why: settings rows are enums, a text field needs its own editor.
- Comments carry `agent: true` and no `source` field.
  Why: the TUI only needs "is this an agent".

### Reload and edits

- `File > Reload` discards unsaved edits without a question.
  The only warning is the badge `FILE CHANGED ON DISK`.
  Other option: a confirm dialog, or a diff view.
  Why: the menu entry is the explicit "take the disk" choice.
- The checkbox key (`x`, space, click) edits the markdown directly and marks the file dirty.
  `ctrl+s` writes it.
  `q` warns once, a second `q` quits and drops the edits.
  Other option: an edit mode, or a comment that recommends the edit.
- Hidden frontmatter is done with a "first visible line" in the viewport, not by removing lines.
  Cost: one blank first row when the line after the fence is empty.
  Why: screen rows stay 1:1 with document lines, so clicks and comments need no remap.

### Screen and colors

- The TUI palette is a pastel set, the only palette.
  Other option: keep the old VS Code-like palette and use pastel only for recordings.
- `Cursor > Highlight line` colors every screen row of the cursor line, wrapped rows included.
  Other option: only the row with the caret.
- The comment slab is `#303330`, the cursor-line slab `#252725`, both are extra palette entries.
  Other option: darken only the comment slab.
  Why: the comment slab must stay the more visible of the two.
- A wrapped paragraph in flow mode hides its continuation lines.
  A comment on a hidden continuation line loses its gutter marker while flow is on.
  Other option: show a count on the first row of the paragraph.
- Drag-select maps the first selected screen row to a document line the same way a click does.
  Wrapped or hidden rows above it are not counted.
  Other option: a row-to-line table built during render.
- A table wider than the pane overflows as one long line.
  Other option: shorten the widest columns.
- Table alignment cycles only from a click on the header or separator row.
  A click on a body cell only moves the cursor.
  Why: a click to focus a row must not edit the file.
- The default glyphs: comment `✦`, caret `>`, checkbox `[x]`.
  They cycle from the View menu.

### Menus and keys

- View toggles have no key chords.
  They are reached from the menu bar, the palette, or help.
- Booleans that change rendering live in `View`.
  Value cyclers (margin, crumb depth, beta flags) live in `Settings`.
  Other option: one settings palette for everything.
- View toggles are session-only.
  The config file seeds them but is never written.
- The inline comment toggles (agent, own) live in the Comments menu.
  Align and time live only in the settings popup.
  The spec said all four in both.
- The modal takes every key while it is open.
  Escape and enter are handled by the modal.
  Typing goes to the focused input through OpenTUI.
- `shift+enter` for a newline in the comment box needs a terminal that reports shift on enter (kitty protocol).
  On a legacy terminal it saves instead.

## Part 2. Detours that cost time

Each item says what went wrong and how to avoid it.
The full list is in `PAPERCUTS.md`.
This is the part that still applies to work today.

- OpenTUI paints a full-width styled row into the row below.
  The ANSI emitter skips the reset at the last column and never sends "dim off".
  A dim `────` rule made the title under it dim after a scroll.
  Rule: full-width rows use color only, no attributes.
- Two writes of the same file at the same time used one temporary name.
  The first rename took the file, the second failed with `ENOENT`.
  Rule: every temporary file gets its own name, and a loop saves once, not per item.
- A promise that nobody awaits or catches shows the OpenTUI log console over the page.
  That is the "console focused" screen you saw.
  Rule: every background promise in the TUI goes through `safe()`, which shows the error as a badge.
- The comment box never grew while typing because `TextareaRenderable` never sends an `input` event.
  Use `onContentChange`.
  Its `virtualLineCount` also stays at 1, so count wrapped rows yourself.
- A renderable that was resized in this tick still reports its old height.
  Pass the new height yourself when you center it.
- `fs.watch` on one file dies after the first atomic save, because the editor replaces the file.
  Watch the directory.
  Under Bun a directory watch reports only the temporary name, so do not filter the markdown by name.
- Headless TUI runs: pipe keys with sleeps into `script -qec "stty rows N cols M; bun src/bin.ts <file>"`.
  Reconstruct the screen from cursor moves, because OpenTUI repaints only changed cells.
  A flat text scrape misleads.
- `jumpToLine` re-anchors the window and makes the page jump.
  Use `moveCursor` when the window must stay.
- Wrapping by UTF-16 unit splits emoji and crashes the encoder.
  Wrap on code points with display widths.
- `pkill -f "bun src/bin.ts"` also kills the shell that runs it.
  Anchor the pattern: `^bun src/bin.ts`.
- OSC-52 copy must go through the renderer, `process.stdout.write` never reaches the terminal.

## Part 3. Last open review item

- The scroll position is kept as two numbers: the source line at the top of the screen, plus the rows of that line hidden above the top.
  A `Caret` type already holds that pair.
  The tidy-up is to store one `Caret` instead of two numbers.
  Nothing on screen changes.
  Parked, no action planned unless you want it.
